LESSON: WRITING 2.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.5: Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can we become better at spelling?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy - self-awareness: The learner sorts out their priorities as they search online or offline for examples of

abbreviations.

● Communication and collaboration writing clearly: The learner advances the skill of spelling while designing charts and

posters/braille cards featuring abbreviations, acronyms, words with affixes, frequently misspelled and easily confused

words.

Values:
● Responsibility - diligence: The learner diligently uses the internet while searching for abbreviations and frequently

confused words.

● Peace: The learner works with peers peacefully online as they search for abbreviations, acronyms, frequently misspelled

and easily confused words.

25

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Socio-economic issues - Climate change: The learner brings out issues on climate change in self-written paragraphs.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print texts

● Braille texts

● Electronic reading materials

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Audio visual clips

Suggested Skills:

● Identifying frequently misspelled and easily confused words in written texts,

● Using acronyms, commonly misspelled and easily confused words in sentences,

● Applying spelling rules to write words with affixes,
